nomenclature.author: Lippold, Hans (1980)
nomenclature.etymology:
-
Cascabela
: From the Spanish
cascabel, cascabela
for a small bell, jingle bell, in reference to the flowers of some species of the genus.
-
Thevetia
: For Andre Thevet (1502-1592), a French traveller in Brazil and Guiana.
nomenclature.etymology_html:
- Cascabela : From the Spanish cascabel, cascabela for a small bell, jingle bell, in reference to the flowers of some species of the genus.
- Thevetia : For Andre Thevet (1502-1592), a French traveller in Brazil and Guiana.

stem_bark.text: The bark of Cascabela thevetia is light brown-coloured and rough. It flakes off in thin and irregular scales.
stem_bark.text_html: The bark of Cascabela thevetia is light brown-coloured and rough. It flakes off in thin and irregular scales.

seed.text: The seeds of Cascabela thevetia are enclosed into a subellipsoid stone. The stone is brown-coloured with a longitudinal and a transversal furrow. Each stone contains 2 seeds. The seeds are whitish-coloured and subglobose. They are about 1.3 cm in diameter with a small beak.
seed.text_html:
The seeds of Cascabela thevetia are enclosed into a subellipsoid stone. The stone is brown-coloured with a longitudinal and a transversal furrow. Each stone contains 2 seeds.
The seeds are whitish-coloured and subglobose. They are about 1.3 cm in diameter with a small beak.

fruit.text: The fruit of Cascabela thevetia is a globose drupe . The fruit is about 3-4 cm across with a 3-4 cm long peduncle. It is green-coloured turning dark brown blackish-coloured when fully ripe. Each drupe contains one stone.
fruit.text_html: The fruit of Cascabela thevetia is a globose drupe. The fruit is about 3-4 cm across with a 3-4 cm long peduncle. It is green-coloured turning dark brown blackish-coloured when fully ripe. Each drupe contains one stone.

images.caption: Cascabela thevetia unripe fruit transversal section

flower.text: The flowers of Cascabela thevetia are grouped in axillary few-flowered cymes. The calyx is composed of 5 triangular sepals. They are 1 cm long and 0.4 mm wide. The calyx is light green-coloured and glabrous. The corolla is composed of 5 yellow-coloured petals (sometimes white or pink-coloured). The petals are connate at the base into a 2.5 cm long tube. The corolla-lobes are obovate and overlapping, 4 cm long and 3.5 cm wide. The androecium is composed of 5 included stamens at the throat of the tube. The pistil is stout and very short with a conical and large stigma .
flower.text_html:
The flowers of Cascabela thevetia are grouped in axillary few-flowered cymes.
The calyx is composed of 5 triangular sepals. They are 1 cm long and 0.4 mm wide. The calyx is light green-coloured and glabrous.
The corolla is composed of 5 yellow-coloured petals (sometimes white or pink-coloured). The petals are connate at the base into a 2.5 cm long tube. The corolla-lobes are obovate and overlapping, 4 cm long and 3.5 cm wide.
The androecium is composed of 5 included stamens at the throat of the tube.
The pistil is stout and very short with a conical and large stigma.

images.caption: Cascabela thevetia flower, bud and young fruit

leaf.text: The leaves of Cascabela thevetia grow alternately on the stem (spirally arranged). The leaf is simple, bright green-coloured above and paler beneath. The leaf is coriaceous, glossy and glabrous on both sides. The leaves are subsessile. The leaf of Cascabela thevetia is 12-15 cm long and about 1 cm wide. The shape of the blade is linear-lanceolate, the apex is acute, the base is cuneate and the margins are entire.

images.caption: Cascabela thevetia leaf (upper and lower sides)

habit.text: Cascabela thevetia is a thornless, small-sized and evergreen tree growing up to 6-8 m high.
habit.text_html: Cascabela thevetia is a thornless, small-sized and evergreen tree growing up to 6-8 m high.

distribution.text: Not specified. Cascabela thevetia is native to tropical America. The plant is cultivated as an ornamental tree and naturalized throughout the tropics.
distribution.text_html:
• Ecology :

    Not specified.

  • Distribution :

    Cascabela thevetia is native to tropical America. The plant is cultivated as an ornamental tree and naturalized throughout the tropics.

reproduction_dispersal.text: Cascabela thevetia is bisexual (each flower of each individual has both male and female structures). Cascabela thevetia is pollinated by a wide variety of insects and sunbirds (in India). The seeds of Cascabela thevetia are mainly dispersed by frugivorous birds and mammals.

  • Seed dispersal :

    The seeds of Cascabela thevetia are mainly dispersed by frugivorous birds and mammals.

culinary.text: All parts of Cascabela thevetia are poisonous, extremely toxic (cardiac glycosides).
culinary.text_html: All parts of Cascabela thevetia are poisonous, extremely toxic (cardiac glycosides).

reforestation.text: Cascabela thevetia can be planted in the sun or half shade. It is drought resistant and it will grow in a wide variety of situations and soils but all soils need to be free draining. The species is propagated by seeds or by cuttings. 12 hours of soaking in water accelerates the germination process.
